video_goal: Demonstrate how to physically insert a SIM card and verify cellular network connection on a US-unlocked Google Pixel 10.
single_prompt: An over-the-shoulder view shows hands picking up a US-unlocked base model Google Pixel 10 with a distinctive horizontal rear camera bar, a metal SIM ejector tool, and a nano-SIM card from a smooth wooden desk under bright, even studio lighting. The camera moves to a close-up as the phone is held sideways, and a metal SIM ejector tool is brought toward the small circular hole next to the USB-C port. In an extreme close-up, the tip of the metal SIM ejector tool presses firmly into the hole, popping the SIM tray out about two millimeters. The camera pulls back to a close-up as thumb and index finger pinch the protruding edge of the SIM tray and pull it completely out. From a top-down view, the empty SIM tray rests on the desk while fingers carefully align and drop a nano-SIM card into it, ensuring the gold contacts face upward. The camera returns to a close-up as fingers guide the loaded SIM tray back into the bottom slot of the Pixel 10, pushing it flush. In a first-person view, the right thumb presses the side power button, illuminating the screen to the default lock screen. A screen capture angle shows a finger swiping up to unlock the device and tapping the gear-shaped Settings app icon. The finger then taps the 'Network & internet' option at the top of the menu. Next, the finger taps the 'SIMs' menu item, revealing the newly recognized cellular carrier's name with a toggle switch turned on. An extreme close-up focuses on the top right corner of the phone's status bar as the hollow signal triangle fills with solid white bars and a '5G' logo appears. Finally, an over-the-shoulder view shows the user holding the fully set up Google Pixel 10, swiping back to the home screen while the active cellular signal remains visible, all resting on a smooth wooden desk under bright, even studio lighting.
